newsitem.title: USA: Dow posts its second largest point gain ever.
newsitem.headline: Dow posts its second largest point gain ever.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average soared Tuesday to post its second largest daily gain ever as investors rushed to the relative safety of big-name companies.
The world's most widely watched stock index ended up 173.38 points, or 2.60 percent, at 6,833.59.
The gain was second in point terms only to the 187-point leap that took placed two days after the "Black Monday" stock market crash of Oct. 19, 1987, when the 30-stock Dow crumbled 508 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 1,533 to 955 on active volume of 501 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Despite the powerhouse performance by blue chips, analysts were on the edge of their seats, eyeing the mixed performance in the broader market. Indeed, buyers appeared extremely focused and largely shunned mid- and small-name stocks.

"People are looking for companies with strong earnings and strong balance sheets," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "Money is moving towards predictability rather than projections."
Seasonal factors may have contributed to the sudden burst of buying, analysts said.

"A lot of the money we saw today is money that was put in retirement accounts by the April 15 (tax) deadline," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "And that money's going directly into index funds."
It was on April 15 that the Dow last managed a rally of this magnitude, posting a 135-point rally that then stood as the index's second best.
Again on Tuesday, there was evidence of clear investor preference for safety over speculation.
"What's very clear in the composition of mutual fund flows is that investors have become more risk averse," said Doug Cliggott, U.S. equity strategist at J.P. Morgan.
"If you look at the past four weeks, 60 percent of the new money is going to income or growth and income funds," he said.
Such funds, and the stocks they invest in, offer a combination of healthy dividend yields and lower volatilty that investors crave during periods of instability, Cliggott said.

"I'm somewhat suspicious of the sustainability of this rally in the Dow," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at Everen Securities. "We're still in woeful shape in terms of breadth. This recovery still is extremely focused on the Dow."
If the Dow were to rebound into record territory but leave the rest of the market behind, that would set up stocks for a new, perhaps harsher round of selling, analysts said.

"The worst possible thing, in my opinion, would be for the Dow to make straight up new highs here," said Ralph Bloch, chief technical analyst at Raymond James. "This is not the recipe for a healthy advance."
The Dow last set a record high on March 11, with a close of 7,085.16.
Other analysts agreed, opting to await a clearer picture before predicting clear sailing.
"For this market to resume to the upside, it has to go back to the look and feel we had," said Nie. "That means it needs more volume and it has to resume the breadth it had."
Dow components AlliedSignal Inc., Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co., Coca-Cola Co. and United Technologies Inc., each rose more than 5 percent.

Drug stocks were also strong, led by Bristol-Myers Squibb Co., which jumped 3-5/8 to 63-1/2 after reporting earnings that beat Wall Street estimates. Merck & Co. gained 2-3/4 to 89-1/4 and Pfizer Inc. climbed 2-7/8 to 91-3/4.
Financial stocks also turned in a solid session, led by BankAmerica Corp., up 3-3/4 to 108-5/8 and Citicorp, up 3 to 105-1/2.
Eagle USA Airfreight Inc. tumbled 8-5/8 to 21-7/8 after the company's second quarter results fell short of Wall Street estimates.

Viacom Inc. fell 3 to 27-3/8. The company said it would issue shares to specifically track the performance of its Blockbuster video chain unit. It also said it expected a decline in first quarter cash flow at Blockbuster.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 8.79 points to 1,212.74.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 14.24 points to 774.61. The American Stock Exchange index fell 6.51 to 544.96.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 6.44 to 405.84. The average share was up 64 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,300.287 up 101.37 or 1.41 percent.
